slides.copy:
We’re not married yet.
But try telling that to our habits.
slides.scene: Morning at an airy contemporary office-lobby cafe. Aachu and Zuv keep walking side by side, not posing. Aachu casually straightens Zuv's slightly twisted office ID lanyard with her right hand at the same moment Zuv passes her the plain takeaway coffee he already ordered with his left. Their reciprocal habit must be unmistakable even with the copy hidden. Exactly two people; all four arms and hands coherent; one coffee and one unreadable ID card. Place them in the lower two-thirds beneath generous text space.
slides.emotion: automatic familiarity, tiny knowing smiles, morning warmth

slides.copy:
Every plan starts with:
“Ek minute, usse poochna padega.”
slides.scene: Daytime in Zuv's office break area. Exactly two friends are visibly waiting in front of him—one seated forward at a small table, one standing beside it—midway through proposing an evening plan. Zuv gives them a natural one-minute palm with one hand while turning slightly aside and raising his phone to call Aachu before agreeing. The friends' expectant body language and his pause make the decision dependency readable without speech bubbles. Exactly three people; no view of Aachu.
slides.emotion: matter-of-fact habit, friends mildly amused, Zuv unembarrassed

slides.copy:
Every small decision becomes
a two-person meeting.
slides.scene: Early evening in the same home that appears in Slide 6, at a dining table near the living room. Aachu and Zuv sit opposite each other as if in a comically serious board meeting. Papers, two notebooks, pens, two mugs and an open laptop surround just two tiny curtain-fabric swatches at the centre. Both lean in and point toward the swatches with concentrated grown-up seriousness. The absurd scale mismatch—lots of meeting apparatus for one tiny home decision—is the joke. Exactly two people.
slides.emotion: dead-serious teamwork with a subtle playful undertone

slides.scene: Later in the same Slide 6 living room. Zuv sits alone in the dominant foreground at the coffee table, reading one troubling work document beside the open laptop. One hand presses his forehead while the other clearly owns the single page. Aachu has just entered at the far edge of the room and stops when she notices his face; she does not touch him, the paper or the laptop yet. The composition clearly says the problem begins with one person.
slides.emotion: Zuv privately worried; Aachu alert and observant

slides.scene: A direct continuation in the same living room. The same one work document and laptop remain centred on the coffee table. Aachu and Zuv now occupy opposite ends of the beige sofa in mirrored thinking postures: both lean forward, elbow on knee, hand near forehead, staring at the same single problem. Keep them physically separate but emotionally synchronized. Exactly two people and one problem document.
slides.emotion: shared overthinking, mutual concern, no anger yet

slides.scene: Use the creator-approved existing Slide 6 final unchanged.

slides.copy:
Then five minutes later:
“Ghar pahunch ke text karna.”
slides.scene: Exactly five minutes after the approved cushion fight, inside the same messy living room and facing the open front door. The green cushions remain scattered and the work papers are still askew, proving no reset or reconciliation. Zuv is at the threshold putting on one shoe and lifting his dark office bag to leave for his own home. Aachu stays several feet behind beside the sofa with stiff shoulders and an averted irritated face, calling after him without approaching. Zuv pauses just enough to hear, but his torso, hips and leading foot remain pointed out through the door. This is departure, never return.
slides.emotion: argument unresolved; care leaks through irritation

slides.scene: Continue the same departure from a new reverse corridor angle behind and slightly beside Zuv. He is now walking away down the apartment corridor with his dark office bag, shoulders still tight and an unsmiling three-quarter profile. Through the open doorway behind him, Aachu sharply picks up one fallen green cushion and turns her torso away into the room. Both bodies point away from each other; neither approaches and Zuv is not coming back. Preserve the doorway and apartment continuity.
slides.emotion: real lingering anger with visible emotional distance

slides.scene: Later that night inside the same apartment, Aachu sits alone on the beige sofa. The room is only partly reset: two green cushions are back but one remains on the floor, and the same work document is still askew on the coffee table. Her brows stay tight and posture guarded, yet she presses her phone to her ear after placing a call to check on Zuv. She is not smiling. Exactly one visible person; do not show Zuv or a split screen.
slides.emotion: still irritated, unable not to care

slides.scene: Night outside Zuv's own separate apartment door, visibly different from Aachu's home. Zuv stands alone with the same dark office bag, phone pressed to one ear as he answers Aachu's call, while his other hand unlocks his own front door. His expression softens only slightly; no smile, ring close-up, wedding symbol or shared-home implication. The separate doorway is the visible proof that they are not married yet.
slides.emotion: distance softened by relief, still understated

slides.copy:
Shaadi abhi baaki hai.
Par “hum” toh kab ke ban chuke hain.
slides.scene: The next morning returns to the airy office-lobby cafe geography of Slide 1 as a visual match cut. Aachu arrives holding Zuv's forgotten office ID card in her right hand while Zuv simultaneously slides her already-ordered plain coffee toward her with his left. They meet mid-step and exchange both things at once, without discussion or romantic posing. Their small lived-in look acknowledges that yesterday's fight did not erase the automatic 'us'. Exactly two people, one coffee and one unreadable ID card.
slides.emotion: quiet belonging, gentle recognition, earned warmth
